docs.title: What is WaldOT?
docs.text:
WaldOT is a Digital Twin Engine that creates a living bridge between:

  • OPC UA (industrial automation standard)
  • Apache TinkerPop (graph database framework)

This enables:

  • Real-time bidirectional synchronization between OPC UA and graph databases
  • Complex graph queries on industrial data using Gremlin
  • Event-driven automation with the rules engine
  • Edge computing capabilities for low-latency processing

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
1. Unified OT/IT Data Model
  2. OPC UA Objects → TinkerPop Vertices
  3. OPC UA References → Graph Edges

  4. OPC UA Variables → Vertex Properties

  5. Powerful Graph Queries

  6. Gremlin query language for complex traversals
  7. Real-time queries on live industrial data

  8. Graph algorithms (PageRank, shortest path, community detection)

  9. Event-Driven Rules Engine

  10. IF-THEN-THAT rules with JEXL expressions
  11. Priority-based event processing
  12. Hysteresis deduplication

  13. Full graph access in rule conditions and actions

  14. Data Generation & Simulation

  15. 6 algorithms (random, sinusoidal, triangular, etc.)
  16. Perfect for testing without physical hardware

  17. Thousands of concurrent generators with virtual threads

  18. Edge-First Architecture

  19. Runs on-device (RTUs, industrial PCs, edge gateways)
  20. Low latency, offline capable
  21. Bandwidth efficient

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: WaldOT is a Digital Twin Engine that bridges the gap between Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT) by creating a bidirectional, real-time synchronization between OPC UA industrial systems and Apache TinkerPop graph databases.

docs.title: Business Value Proposition
docs.text:
• Unified Data Model: Single source of truth for industrial and analytical data
  • Real-Time Insights: Complex graph queries on live OPC UA data without ETL pipelines
  • Edge Computing: Low-latency processing directly on industrial devices
  • Reduced Integration Costs: Standard protocols (OPC UA + Gremlin) eliminate custom integrations
  • Scalability: From single devices to distributed enterprise deployments
  • Future-Proof: Built on open standards (OPC UA, Apache TinkerPop, Java 26)

docs.title: Layer 1: OPC UA Server (Industrial Interface)
docs.text:
Technology: Eclipse Milo OPC UA SDK

Purpose: Expose industrial data using the OPC UA standard protocol

Capabilities:

  • Full OPC UA server implementation (binary protocol, security, subscriptions)
  • Standard OPC UA address space with Objects, Variables, References
  • Event system for real-time notifications
  • Security: X.509 certificates, user authentication, encryption
  • Compatible with all OPC UA clients (UaExpert, Prosys, custom applications)

Deployment Scenarios:

  • Standalone OPC UA server for legacy system integration
  • Gateway between proprietary protocols and OPC UA
  • Edge device for local data aggregation

docs.title: Layer 2: TinkerPop Graph Database (Analytical Engine)
docs.text:
Technology: Apache TinkerPop 3.x

Purpose: Represent industrial data as a queryable graph structure

Capabilities:

  • Vertices (nodes) represent industrial objects (machines, sensors, zones)
  • Edges (relationships) represent connections (contains, monitors, controls)
  • Properties store dynamic data (temperature, pressure, status)
  • Gremlin query language for complex traversals
  • Graph algorithms (PageRank, shortest path, community detection)
  • Multiple storage backends (in-memory, RocksDB, Neo4j, JanusGraph)

Use Cases:

  • Correlation analysis across distant equipment
  • Root cause analysis with graph traversal
  • Asset relationship mapping
  • Predictive maintenance pattern detection

docs.title: Layer 3: Bidirectional Synchronization (Core Innovation)
docs.text:
Purpose: Keep OPC UA and TinkerPop in perfect sync

Synchronization Flow:

OPC UA Client → Write Variable → OPC UA Server
                                      ↓
                                 WaldOT Sync
                                      ↓
                              TinkerPop Graph
                                      ↓
                              Gremlin Listeners
                                      ↓
                              Rules Engine / Analytics

Gremlin Query → Modify Graph → WaldOT Sync
                                      ↓
                              OPC UA Server
                                      ↓
                              OPC UA Clients (notified)

Key Features:

  • Real-time: Changes propagate in milliseconds
  • Bidirectional: Modifications from either side sync to the other
  • Consistent: ACID properties maintained where supported by storage backend
  • Event-driven: Observers and listeners for reactive programming

docs.title: Concurrency Model: Virtual Threads
docs.text:
Technology: Java 26 (Project Loom) Virtual Threads

Why Virtual Threads?

Traditional platform threads:

  • ~1 MB stack size per thread
  • OS-managed scheduling
  • Limited to thousands of threads
  • Blocking I/O blocks OS thread

Virtual threads:

  • ~1 KB stack size per thread
  • JVM-managed scheduling
  • Millions of threads possible
  • Blocking I/O doesn't block OS thread

Impact on WaldOT:

Scenario: 10,000 sensors polling every second

Platform Threads:
- 10,000 threads × 1 MB = ~10 GB RAM
- Context switching overhead
- Not feasible

Virtual Threads:
- 10,000 threads × 1 KB = ~10 MB RAM
- Minimal overhead
- Easily achievable

Design Pattern:

// Each active object (generator, monitor, rule) runs in its own virtual thread
ExecutorService executor = ThreadHelper.newVirtualThreadExecutor();

// Create thousands of concurrent tasks
for (int i = 0; i < 100000; i++) {
    executor.submit(() -> {
        while (active) {
            // Blocking operations are OK in virtual threads
            data = fetchSensorData();  // Blocking I/O
            updateGraph(data);
            Thread.sleep(1000);  // Blocking sleep
        }
    });
}

Benefits:

  • Simple, readable code (no async/await complexity)
  • Massive concurrency with minimal resources
  • Perfect for I/O-bound workloads (sensors, APIs, databases)

docs.title: Scenario 2: Graph Analytics on Industrial Data
docs.text:
Problem: Need complex queries on industrial data (e.g., "find all motors connected to Line 1 in alarm state")

Solution: WaldOT exposes OPC UA as queryable graph

[OPC UA Data] → [WaldOT Graph] → [Gremlin Queries] → [Analytics / BI Tools]

Example Query (Gremlin Server, waldot-plugin-tinkerpop):

// Find all motors in alarm state connected to Line 1
g.V().has('name', 'Line1')
  .out('contains')
  .has('type', 'motor')
  .has('status', 'alarm')
  .values('name')

Benefits:

  • No ETL pipeline required
  • Real-time queries on live data
  • Complex relationship traversal
  • Graph algorithms (PageRank, community detection)

docs.title: Scenario 3: Event-Driven Automation
docs.text:
Problem: Need automated responses to complex conditions

Solution: WaldOT Rules Engine

[Sensors] → [WaldOT Graph] → [Rules Engine] → [Automated Actions]

Example Rule:

// IF temperature > 80 AND pressure > 100 THEN close the inlet valve
var reactor = "g.V().has('id','reactor').next()";
graph.addVertex('id', 'reactor-critical', 'type', 'rules:rule', 'label', 'reactor-critical',
    'condition', reactor + ".value('temperature') > 80.0 && " + reactor + ".value('pressure') > 100.0",
    'action', "g.V().has('id','inlet-valve').next().property('opening', 0.0); log.error('CRITICAL')");

The rule runs when a fire edge notifies it and a rules:compute executes it (see User Guide).

Benefits:

  • Low latency (edge processing)
  • Complex multi-sensor conditions
  • Full graph access in rules
  • Priority-based execution

docs.title: OPC UA Security
docs.text:
• Encryption: TLS 1.2+ for all OPC UA connections
  • Authentication: X.509 certificates, username/password
  • Authorization: Role-based access control (RBAC)
  • PKI: Full Public Key Infrastructure support
  • Security Policies: Sign, SignAndEncrypt, None (configurable)

docs.title: Application Security
docs.text:
• Default Credentials: MUST be changed in production (--factory-password)
  • Anonymous Access: Disable in production (--anonymous-access false)
  • Exec Command: Disable in production (--exec-command-executable false)
  • Network Isolation: Bind to specific interfaces, use firewalls
  • Secrets Management: Use Docker secrets, Kubernetes secrets, or vault

docs.title: When to Use WaldOT
docs.text:
✅ Good Fit:

  • Complex relationship queries needed
  • Multiple data sources to integrate
  • Edge computing requirements
  • Real-time analytics on industrial data
  • Event-driven automation
  • Flexible, evolving data models

❌ Not Ideal:

  • Pure time-series data (use InfluxDB, TimescaleDB)
  • Simple SCADA (use traditional SCADA)
  • No relationship complexity (use SQL database)
  • Extremely high throughput (>100K events/sec sustained)

docs.title: Evaluation Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Do you need complex relationship queries?
  • [ ] Do you have multiple industrial protocols to integrate?
  • [ ] Do you need edge computing capabilities?
  • [ ] Do you need event-driven automation?
  • [ ] Do you have a Java 26 runtime available (or can you run the Docker image)?
  • [ ] Do you have OPC UA infrastructure or plan to adopt it?
  • [ ] Do you need flexible, evolving data models?

If you answered "yes" to 3+ questions, WaldOT is likely a good fit.

docs.title: WaldOT Configuration Reference
docs.text: This page documents every runtime parameter accepted by the WaldOT server (waldot-app). The source of truth is waldot-runner/src/main/java/net/rossonet/agent/AbstractWaldotRunner.java: all options are declared there with Picocli and inherited by net.rossonet.agent.WaldotRunner.

docs.title: How configuration is applied
docs.text:
WaldOT reads its configuration from three sources:

Source Example Notes Command-line options --tcp-port 4840 Primary mechanism, parsed by Picocli. Java system properties -Dwaldot.milo.strategy=base Low-level switches of the namespace module. Bootstrap file --boot-url file:///waldot/boot.conf Initial graph content (see Bootstrap).

Picocli also supports @file argument files (showAtFileInUsageHelp is enabled), so a long option list can be stored in a file and passed as @/path/to/waldot.args.

Environment variables are not used to configure WaldOT: every runtime parameter is a command-line option. In Docker, options are simply appended after the image name (see Docker usage).

Boolean options (--anonymous-access and all *-executable / *-user-executable flags) accept an optional value: --anonymous-access false disables the feature, the option alone (--anonymous-access) means true.

To print the full, always up-to-date option list:

# Docker image
docker run --rm rossonet/waldot:latest --help
# fat jar built with ./gradlew waldot-app:shadowJar
java -jar waldot-app/build/libs/waldot-app-<version>-all.jar --help

docs.title: Network options
docs.text:
Option Short Default Description --tcp-port -tp 12686 TCP port of the OPC UA binary endpoint (opc.tcp://). --https-port -hp 8443 HTTPS port for OPC UA web services. --bind-addresses -ba 0.0.0.0 Comma-separated list of bind addresses. --bind-hostname -bh 127.0.0.1 Hostname published in endpoint URLs and certificates. --endpoint-path -ep /waldot Path component of the endpoint URL.

The resulting endpoint is opc.tcp://<bind-hostname>:<tcp-port><endpoint-path>, for example opc.tcp://127.0.0.1:12686/waldot.

docs.title: Server identity
docs.text: Option Short Default Description --application-name -an WaldOT OPCUA server OPC UA application name. --product-name -pn WaldOT Product name in BuildInfo. --product-uri -pu urn:rossonet:waldot:uaserver Product URI in the application description. --manufacturer-name -mn Zona Autonoma srl Manufacturer name in BuildInfo. --build-number -bn w001 Build number in BuildInfo. --namespace-uri -nu urn:rossonet:waldot:engine URI of the WaldOT namespace.

docs.title: Security and authentication
docs.text:
Option Short Default Description --security-dir -sd .security Directory for certificates, private keys and PKI trust lists (relative to the working directory, /app in Docker). --dns-address-cert -dc 127.0.0.1 DNS name used as Subject Alternative Name of the generated certificate. --anonymous-access -aa true Allow anonymous OPC UA sessions. --factory-username -fu admin Initial administrator user name. --factory-password -fp password123 Initial administrator password. Change it in production.

Production hardening

With the default values anonymous access is enabled, the administrator password is public and the exec command (which runs operating-system commands) is enabled. Always override --anonymous-access, --factory-password and --exec-command-executable outside development.

Known limitation

In the current release --anonymous-access false is parsed and stored in the configuration, but the anonymous identity validators still accept anonymous sessions. Do not rely on this flag alone to protect a server exposed on an untrusted network.

docs.title: Built-in OPC UA commands
docs.text:
Each built-in command is an OPC UA method under the commands folder and is configured by four options with the same pattern: --<cmd>-command-label, --<cmd>-command-description, --<cmd>-command-executable, --<cmd>-command-user-executable.

Command (<cmd>) Default label Default description Purpose about about info about this software Software information. help help list available commands Lists available commands / help files. waldot query run Gremlin query Executes a JEXL expression (with g, graph, log, cmd) on the graph. exec exec run system command Executes an operating-system command.

All *-executable and *-user-executable flags default to true.

Example: disable the exec command entirely

--exec-command-executable false --exec-command-user-executable false

docs.title: Java system properties
docs.text: Property Default Description waldot.milo.strategy optimized Milo strategy used by the namespace: optimized or base (legacy). Unknown values fall back to optimized. waldot.boot.file /tmp/boot.conf Bootstrap file used by OpcFactory.getOpcGraph() (embedded/test usage only, not by the server runner).

docs.title: Bootstrap file
docs.text:
The bootstrap file is loaded at startup from --boot-url. Its format is detected automatically:

  • script mode (recommended): the whole file is one JEXL script with variables, functions, loops and // comments; every statement must end with ;;
  • line mode (legacy): one expression per line, # comments.

The file is executed again by cmd.reset(), which does not remove the existing vertices.

The detailed syntax and detection rules are maintained in waldot-namespace/BOOTSTRAP_CONFIGURATION.md.

docs.title: Docker usage
docs.text:
The image is built from the repository Dockerfile (multi-stage build: eclipse-temurin:26-jdk to compile, eclipse-temurin:26-jre-alpine at runtime):

docker buildx build --load -t rossonet/waldot:latest .

Image layout:

Item Value Working directory /app Libraries /app/lib (waldot-app, generator, rules engine and TinkerPop plugins, dependencies) Help files /app/help (index.txt, author.txt, license.txt) Security directory /app/.security (declared as volume) Bootstrap file /waldot/boot.conf (mount it, default of --boot-url) Exposed ports 12686 (OPC UA TCP), 8443 (HTTPS) User waldot (uid/gid 1000, non-root) Entrypoint java --add-opens ... -cp /app/lib/* net.rossonet.agent.MainAgent Default command empty

Every argument after the image name is passed to WaldOT as an option:

docker run -p 4840:4840 \
  -v "$PWD/boot.conf:/waldot/boot.conf:ro" \
  rossonet/waldot:latest \
  --tcp-port 4840 \
  --anonymous-access false \
  --factory-password 'S3cure!' \
  --exec-command-executable false

The same applies to command: in Docker Compose:

services:
  waldot:
    image: rossonet/waldot:latest
    ports:
      - "4840:4840"
    volumes:
      - waldot-security:/app/.security
      - ./boot.conf:/waldot/boot.conf:ro
    command:
      - "--tcp-port"
      - "4840"
volumes:
  waldot-security:

JVM options (heap size, system properties) are supplied through the standard JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS variable, read by the java launcher itself:

docker run -e JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS="-Xmx2g -Dwaldot.milo.strategy=optimized" rossonet/waldot:latest

If no file is mounted on /waldot/boot.conf the server starts with an empty graph and logs the bootstrap configuration is empty or null.

Host directories mounted for writing (for example a bind mount on /app/.security) must be writable by uid 1000.

Ready-to-use Compose files are available in waldot-app/examples.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: net.rossonet.agent.MainAgent terminates the JVM with the code returned by Picocli: 0 on normal shutdown, 1 for an exception during execution, 2 for invalid command-line arguments.

docs.title: 1. WaldotGraph
docs.text:
The main interface combining TinkerPop Graph with OPC UA integration.

// Open graph
WaldotGraph graph = OpcFactory.getOpcGraph(
    "file:///tmp/waldot.db",
    new LoggerHistoryStrategy()
);

// Add vertex
Vertex v = graph.addVertex();
v.property("label", "sensor1");
v.property("temperature", 25.5);

// Query
List<Vertex> sensors = graph.traversal()
    .V()
    .has("label", "sensor1")
    .toList();

// Close
graph.close();

docs.title: 2. WaldotVertex
docs.text:
Represents both a TinkerPop Vertex and an OPC UA Object.

WaldotVertex sensor = (WaldotVertex) graph.addVertex();
sensor.property("label", "temp-sensor");
sensor.property("value", 20.0);

// Add edge
WaldotVertex zone = (WaldotVertex) graph.addVertex();
zone.property("label", "production-zone");
sensor.addEdge("located-in", zone);

// Observe property changes
sensor.addPropertyObserver((vertex, key, oldValue, newValue) -> {
    System.out.println(key + " changed: " + oldValue + " → " + newValue);
});

    .has("type", "sensor")
    .toList();

// Find sensors in alarm

    .has("type", "sensor")
    .has("status", "alarm")
    .values("label")
    .toList();

// Complex traversal

    .has("label", "Line1")
    .out("contains")
    .has("type", "motor")
    .has("status", "alarm")
    .path()
    .by("label")
    .toList();

docs.title: Plugin Development
docs.text:
Plugins are discovered at startup: a top-level class annotated with @WaldotPlugin, with a public no-argument constructor, located in a package under net.rossonet.waldot, plugin or plugins, usually extending AbstractPluginListener. It registers vertex types (registerTypeNode(...)), edge types (registerTypeEdge(...)) and commands (registerCommand(...)) in initialize(WaldotNamespace).

The complete, verified walkthrough (project setup, vertex hooks, custom edges, commands, packaging in the Docker image, tests) is in the Integration Guide.

docs.title: Working with the base plugins

docs.title: WaldOT Integration Guide: Writing a Plugin
docs.text:
This guide explains how to extend WaldOT with a plugin: a Java library that adds new active vertex types, edge types and commands to the graph. Every example on this page has been compiled against the libraries of the rossonet/waldot image and executed in a container.

The built-in plugins of the waldot-app distribution are the reference implementations:

Plugin Module Vertex types Edge types Commands (folder) Generator plugins/waldot-plugin-generator sim:generator, sim:event-generator — create generator, create event generator (simulator) Rules engine plugins/waldot-plugin-rules-engine rules:rule, rules:compute rules:execute create rule, create compute, create compute monitored edge, showcases (rules) TinkerPop plugins/waldot-plugin-tinkerpop gremlin — create gremlin server (tinkerpop)

docs.title: 1. What a plugin can do
docs.text:
In WaldOT every vertex of the graph is also an OPC UA object and every vertex property is an OPC UA variable. A plugin contributes:

  • vertex types: a Java class (subclass of AbstractOpcVertex) plus an OPC UA ObjectType. When a vertex is created with type = <your label> WaldOT asks your plugin to build it. The vertex can run code: react to property writes, receive notifications through fire edges, run background threads, publish OPC UA events;
  • edge types: labels for which your plugin is notified when an edge is added or removed, with the possibility to veto the creation;
  • commands: OPC UA methods under the Commands folder that are also callable from bootstrap scripts, rule actions and the query console.

Everything a plugin does is visible from any OPC UA client: the vertex variables, the events it posts, the commands it exposes.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
At startup WaldotOpcUaServer scans the class path for top-level classes annotated with @WaldotPlugin in these packages (and their sub-packages):

net.rossonet.waldot    plugin    plugins

The class must implement PluginListener (in practice: extend AbstractPluginListener) and have a public no-argument constructor.

Warning

A class in any other package (for example com.mycompany.waldot) is not discovered. Use plugins.<vendor>.<name> for third-party plugins.

The log confirms the discovery:

INFO net.rossonet.waldot.opc.WaldotOpcUaServer - Found plugin: plugins.example.ThresholdPlugin
INFO net.rossonet.waldot.namespaces.HomunculusNamespace - Registering commands from plugin ThresholdPlugin

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Phase Method What to do Registration initialize(WaldotNamespace) Register vertex types, edge types and commands. Called once, before the OPC UA server starts. Command registration getCommands() Returns the commands to publish (filled by registerCommand(...)). Read right after initialize. Start start() Called just before the bootstrap file is executed (and again after a namespace reset). Vertex creation containsVertexType(label), getVertexTypeNode(label), containsVertexTypeNode(nodeId), createVertex(...) Handled by AbstractPluginListener once the type is registered. Edge creation / removal containsEdgeType(label), notifyAddEdge(...), notifyRemoveEdge(...) Called only for the edge types you registered. Throw PluginBlockingException to refuse an edge. Reset reset() Namespace reset: clear plugin state; the bootstrap runs again afterwards. Shutdown stop() Stop background activity of the plugin.

docs.title: 3. Project setup
docs.text: All WaldOT modules target Java 26. A plugin only needs waldot-api at compile time: it brings Eclipse Milo, Apache TinkerPop and the WaldOT base classes.

docs.title: Option A: module inside the WaldOT repository
docs.text:
1. Create plugins/waldot-plugin-<name>/ with src/main/java/....

  2. Register it in settings.gradle:

    include 'waldot-plugin-<name>'
project(':waldot-plugin-<name>').projectDir = file('plugins/waldot-plugin-<name>')

  3. Minimal build.gradle (same layout as the built-in plugins):

    group = 'net.rossonet.waldot'
version = "${rootProject.version}"

apply plugin: 'java-library'

java {
    sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_26
    targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_26
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
    maven { url 'https://jitpack.io' }
}

dependencies {
    implementation project(':waldot-deps')
    api project(':waldot-api')
    testImplementation project(':waldot-namespace')
    testImplementation testFixtures(project(':waldot-client'))
    testImplementation(platform('org.junit:junit-bom:5.13.1'))
    testImplementation('org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter')
    testRuntimeOnly('org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher')
}

  4. Add it to the application in waldot-app/build.gradle:

    implementation project(':waldot-plugin-<name>')

    The next docker buildx build produces an image that contains it.

docs.title: Option B: external jar added to an existing image
docs.text:
The image starts WaldOT with the class path /app/lib/*: any jar placed in /app/lib is loaded and scanned for plugins.

  1. Compile against the WaldOT libraries (for example the jars of the image):

    mkdir -p lib
docker run --rm --entrypoint sh -v "$PWD/lib:/out" rossonet/waldot:latest \
  -c 'cp /app/lib/*.jar /out/'
javac --release 26 -cp "lib/*" -d out $(find src -name '*.java')
jar --create --file my-plugin.jar -C out .

  2. Mount the jar (development):

    docker run -p 12686:12686 \
  -v "$PWD/my-plugin.jar:/app/lib/my-plugin.jar:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/boot.conf:/waldot/boot.conf:ro" \
  rossonet/waldot:latest

    or build a derived image (production):

    FROM rossonet/waldot:latest
COPY my-plugin.jar /app/lib/

Third-party libraries not already present in /app/lib must be shipped with the plugin (extra jars in /app/lib or a shaded jar).

docs.title: 4. Step by step: a threshold plugin
docs.text:
The example adds the vertex type example:threshold. The vertex compares its value with its limit, keeps alarm and exceeded-count up to date and posts an OPC UA event on every transition. value can be written by an OPC UA client, by a rule, by a Gremlin query or, more interestingly, by a link-to edge coming from another vertex.

src/main/java/plugins/example/
├── ThresholdPlugin.java         plugin: registers type and command
├── ThresholdVertex.java         active vertex
└── CreateThresholdCommand.java  OPC UA / console command

docs.title: 4.1 The plugin class
docs.text:
package plugins.example;

import net.rossonet.waldot.api.annotation.WaldotPlugin;
import net.rossonet.waldot.api.models.WaldotNamespace;
import net.rossonet.waldot.plugin.AbstractPluginListener;

@WaldotPlugin
public class ThresholdPlugin extends AbstractPluginListener {

    /** Value of the "type" property that selects this plugin. */
    public static final String TYPE_LABEL = "example:threshold";

    /** Folder of the plugin commands under the OPC UA "Commands" node. */
    public static final String COMMAND_DIRECTORY = "example";

    @Override
    public void initialize(final WaldotNamespace waldotNamespace) {
        super.initialize(waldotNamespace);
        commands.clear();
        // OPC UA ObjectType + Java class + type label
        registerTypeNode(ThresholdVertex.class, "ExampleThresholdObjectType",
                "Example Threshold", TYPE_LABEL);
        waldotNamespace.getOpcuaServer().updateReferenceTypeTree();
        // OPC UA method Commands/example/"create threshold",
        // console function example_create_threshold
        registerCommand(new CreateThresholdCommand(waldotNamespace));
        logger.info("Example threshold plugin initialized");
    }
}

registerTypeNode(vertexClass, typeNodeId, displayName, typeLabel):

  • creates the OPC UA ObjectType ObjectTypes/<typeNodeId> (subtype of BaseObjectType) with a Label variable;
  • calls the static method generateParameters(WaldotNamespace, UaObjectTypeNode) of the vertex class (by reflection) to describe the other variables of the type;
  • binds typeLabel to the class: AbstractPluginListener.createVertex(...) then instantiates the class through the standard constructor shown below.

If the vertex needs extra constructor arguments (for example a shared executor), override createVertex(...) as WaldotGeneratorPlugin does for sim:generator.

docs.title: 4.2 The vertex class
docs.text:
package plugins.example;

import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.sdk.server.model.objects.BaseEventType;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.sdk.server.nodes.UaNode;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.sdk.server.nodes.UaNodeContext;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.sdk.server.nodes.UaObjectTypeNode;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.NodeIds;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.builtin.DataValue;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.builtin.LocalizedText;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.builtin.NodeId;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.builtin.QualifiedName;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.builtin.unsigned.UByte;
import org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.builtin.unsigned.UInteger;

import net.rossonet.waldot.api.PluginListener;
import net.rossonet.waldot.api.models.WaldotGraph;
import net.rossonet.waldot.api.models.WaldotNamespace;
import net.rossonet.waldot.opc.AbstractOpcVertex;

public class ThresholdVertex extends AbstractOpcVertex implements AutoCloseable {

    public static final String ALARM = "alarm";
    public static final String COUNT = "exceeded-count";
    public static final String LIMIT = "limit";
    public static final String VALUE = "value";

    /** Called by registerTypeNode(...): variables of the OPC UA ObjectType. */
    public static void generateParameters(final WaldotNamespace namespace,
            final UaObjectTypeNode typeNode) {
        PluginListener.addParameterToTypeNode(namespace, typeNode, LIMIT, NodeIds.Double, "alarm threshold");
        PluginListener.addParameterToTypeNode(namespace, typeNode, VALUE, NodeIds.Double, "monitored value");
        PluginListener.addParameterToTypeNode(namespace, typeNode, ALARM, NodeIds.Boolean, "true when value > limit");
        PluginListener.addParameterToTypeNode(namespace, typeNode, COUNT, NodeIds.Int64,
                "number of times the limit was exceeded");
    }

    private boolean inAlarm = false;

    /** Constructor signature required by AbstractPluginListener.createVertex(...). */
    public ThresholdVertex(final WaldotGraph graph, final UaNodeContext context, final NodeId nodeId,
            final QualifiedName browseName, final LocalizedText displayName, final LocalizedText description,
            final UInteger writeMask, final UInteger userWriteMask, final UByte eventNotifier, final long version,
            final Object[] propertyKeyValues) {
        super(graph, context, nodeId, browseName, displayName, description, writeMask, userWriteMask,
                eventNotifier, version);
        // managed properties: typed, with default value and optional validation
        addManagedProperty(LIMIT, NodeIds.Double, Double.class, false, 100.0, (label, oldValue, newValue) -> {
            if (newValue == null || newValue.isNaN()) {
                throw new PropertyChangeException("limit must be a number");
            }
        }, false, propertyKeyValues);
        addManagedProperty(VALUE, NodeIds.Double, Double.class, false, 0.0, null, false, propertyKeyValues);
        addManagedProperty(ALARM, NodeIds.Boolean, Boolean.class, false, false, null, false, propertyKeyValues);
        addManagedProperty(COUNT, NodeIds.Int64, Long.class, false, 0L, null, false, propertyKeyValues);
    }

    private synchronized void check() {
        final Double value = getRuntimeParameter(VALUE);
        final Double limit = getRuntimeParameter(LIMIT);
        if (value == null || limit == null) {
            return;
        }
        final boolean alarm = value > limit;
        if (alarm != inAlarm) {
            inAlarm = alarm;
            updatePropertyIfChanged(ALARM, alarm);
            if (alarm) {
                final Long count = getRuntimeParameter(COUNT);
                updatePropertyIfChanged(COUNT, (count == null ? 0L : count) + 1);
            }
            // OPC UA event, visible to every client subscribed to the vertex
            sendLogEvent("threshold", (alarm ? "limit exceeded: " : "back to normal: ") + value + " / " + limit,
                    alarm ? 700 : 100);
        }
    }

    /** Required by GremlinElement. */
    @Override
    public Object clone() {
        return new ThresholdVertex(graph, getNodeContext(), getNodeId(), getBrowseName(), getDisplayName(),
                getDescription(), getWriteMask(), getUserWriteMask(), getEventNotifier(), version(),
                getPropertiesAsStringArray());
    }

    @Override
    public void close() {
        // release threads, sockets, files... (nothing to do here)
    }

    /** A "fire" edge pointing to this vertex delivers source events here. */
    @Override
    public void fireEvent(final UaNode node, final BaseEventType event, final int priority) {
        check();
    }

    /** A "fire" edge pointing to this vertex delivers source property changes here. */
    @Override
    public void fireProperty(final UaNode node, final String propertyLabel, final DataValue value,
            final int priority) {
        check();
    }

    /** Every property write (OPC UA client, Gremlin, rule, link edge) passes here. */
    @Override
    public void notifyPropertyValueChanging(final String label, final DataValue value) {
        super.notifyPropertyValueChanging(label, value); // keeps managed properties in sync
        if (VALUE.equals(label) || LIMIT.equals(label)) {
            check();
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void notifyRemoveVertex() {
        close();
    }
}

docs.title: 4.3 The creation command
docs.text:
package plugins.example;

import java.util.List;

import net.rossonet.waldot.api.models.WaldotNamespace;
import net.rossonet.waldot.opc.AbstractCreateVertexCommand;

public class CreateThresholdCommand extends AbstractCreateVertexCommand {

    public CreateThresholdCommand(final WaldotNamespace waldotNamespace) {
        super(waldotNamespace, "create threshold", "Create an example threshold vertex",
                ThresholdPlugin.COMMAND_DIRECTORY, ThresholdPlugin.TYPE_LABEL, Language.ENGLISH,
                List.of(VertexParameter.optional(ThresholdVertex.LIMIT, VariableNodeTypes.Double,
                        "alarm threshold, default 100")));
    }

    @Override
    protected String validate(final List<Object> keyValues) {
        final String limit = findValue(keyValues, ThresholdVertex.LIMIT);
        if (limit != null && Double.parseDouble(limit) < 0) {
            return "the limit must not be negative";
        }
        return null;
    }
}

docs.title: 4.4 Using the new vertex
docs.text:
Bootstrap file (script mode, JEXL syntax):

// a generator feeds the threshold vertex through a link-to edge
gen = graph.addVertex('id', 'gen-1', 'type', 'sim:generator', 'label', 'gen-1', 'directory', 'example',
    'algorithm', 'sinusoidal', 'min', '0', 'max', '200', 'delay', '300');
thr = graph.addVertex('id', 'thr-1', 'type', 'example:threshold', 'label', 'thr-1', 'directory', 'example',
    'limit', '150');
gen.addEdge('feeds', thr, 'type', 'link-to', 'properties-to-monitor', 'data', 'data', 'value');

// the same vertex type created through the plugin command
log.info('created by command: ' + example_create_threshold.exec('thr-2', 'example', '50')[0]);
log.info('invalid: ' + example_create_threshold.exec('thr-3', 'example', '-1')[0]);

Observed result:

INFO AbstractOpcCommand - create vertex with parameters: [type, example:threshold, label, thr-2, directory, example, limit, 50]
INFO CONSOLE - invalid: error: the limit must not be negative

Reading ns=2;s=thr-1 with an OPC UA client every two seconds:

{'limit': 150.0, 'value': 66.17,  'alarm': False, 'exceeded-count': 20, 'type': 'example:threshold'}
{'limit': 150.0, 'value': 136.32, 'alarm': False, 'exceeded-count': 20, 'type': 'example:threshold'}
{'limit': 150.0, 'value': 188.59, 'alarm': True,  'exceeded-count': 22, 'type': 'example:threshold'}

and the folder Commands/example contains the method create threshold.

docs.title: Constructor and identity
docs.text:
• The constructor must have exactly the signature shown above (WaldotGraph, UaNodeContext, NodeId, QualifiedName, LocalizedText, LocalizedText, UInteger, UInteger, UByte, long, Object[]) when you rely on registerTypeNode(...).
  • clone() is abstract in GremlinElement: implement it with the same constructor.
  • propertyKeyValues contains the key/value pairs passed to graph.addVertex(...) or to the command.
  • Reserved keys handled by WaldOT: id (OPC UA identifier, for example ns=2;s=thr-1), type, label, directory (OPC UA folder, levels separated by /), name, description, history flags. label and type cannot be changed after creation.
  • Use lowercase property keys: keys arrive lowercase in notifyPropertyValueChanging and the built-in plugins register their managed properties in lowercase.

docs.title: Managed properties
docs.text:
addManagedProperty(label, opcUaDataType, javaType, isRequired, defaultValue,
        callbackOnChange, isNecessaryRestartVertex, propertyKeyValues);
  • The initial value is taken from propertyKeyValues and converted to javaType (String, Integer, Long, Boolean, Double, Float, Byte, Instant, JSONObject); if absent or not convertible the default is used.
  • Every later write (OPC UA client, Gremlin property(...), rule, link edge) goes through the conversion and, if present, through callbackOnChange; throwing PropertyChangeException rejects the value.
  • getRuntimeParameter(label) returns the current typed value; setRuntimeParameter(label, value) updates it without notifications.
  • property(key, value) / updatePropertyIfChanged(key, value) write a graph property: the OPC UA variable is updated and observers (link-* and fire edges, history) are notified.

docs.title: Reacting to the graph
docs.text:
Hook Triggered by notifyPropertyValueChanging(label, value) Any write of a property of this vertex. Always call super first: it keeps label/type immutable, updates managed properties, notifies observers and history. fireProperty(node, label, value, priority) A fire edge whose source changed one of its properties-to-monitor. fireEvent(node, event, priority) A fire edge whose source posted an OPC UA event. notifyRemoveVertex() The vertex is being removed: stop threads and release resources.

link-to and link-from edges write directly into the target (or source) properties, so a vertex fed by a link edge sees the change in notifyPropertyValueChanging. These hooks run on the caller thread: keep them short and move long or blocking work to a thread of the vertex.

docs.title: Background work
docs.text:
Active vertices that poll a device or produce data run their own loop on a virtual thread, started in the constructor and stopped in close() / notifyRemoveVertex():

runner = Thread.ofVirtual().name("my-vertex-" + getNodeId().toParseableString()).unstarted(this::loop);
runner.start();

Read the parameters at every cycle (as sim:event-generator does) so that OPC UA clients and rules can change them at runtime.

docs.title: Publishing OPC UA events
docs.text:
• sendLogEvent(category, message, severity) posts a SystemEventType event whose source is the vertex (severity 1–1000).
  • postEvent(BaseEventTypeNode) posts an event built with getNamespace().getEventFactory().

Events reach subscribed OPC UA clients and every fire edge leaving the vertex, so they can trigger rules.

docs.title: 6. Custom edge types
docs.text:
Built-in edge behaviors (link-to, link-from, fire) are provided by the namespace. A plugin declares its own edge labels with registerTypeEdge("<prefix>:<name>") in initialize(...). For those labels:

  • notifyAddEdge(edge, source, target, label, type, keyValues) is called after the edge is created; throwing PluginBlockingException removes it and the caller receives an error;
  • notifyRemoveEdge(edge) is called on removal;
  • AbstractPluginListener forwards both notifications to source and target vertices that implement EdgeMonitoredVertex (notifyAddTargetMonitoredEdge, notifyAddSourceMonitoredEdge, ...).

The rules engine uses this mechanism for rules:execute: ComputeVertex implements EdgeMonitoredVertex and refuses the edge when the target is not a rule:

@Override
public void notifyAddTargetMonitoredEdge(WaldotEdge edge, WaldotVertex targetVertex,
        String label, String type, Object[] propertyKeyValues) throws PluginBlockingException {
    if (!RulesEngineConstants.EXECUTE_EDGE_LABEL.equals(type)) {
        return;
    }
    if (!(targetVertex instanceof ComputableFireableAbstractOpcVertex)) {
        throw new PluginBlockingException("The target of a " + type
                + " edge must be a rule vertex, but it is " + targetVertex);
    }
    // ... start serving the rule
}

docs.title: Vertex creation commands
docs.text:
AbstractCreateVertexCommand builds a complete OPC UA method from a list of VertexParameters:

  • inputs: label, directory, then one argument per parameter (VertexParameter.optional(...) / VertexParameter.required(...) with an OPC UA type from VariableNodeTypes);
  • output: result, the NodeId of the new vertex or a message starting with error:;
  • empty inputs are skipped (the vertex uses its defaults), numeric and boolean values are checked, then validate(keyValues) runs your own checks;
  • clone() uses the constructor with the WaldotNamespace as only argument.

docs.title: Where commands appear
docs.text:
Access Name OPC UA method Commands/<directory>/<command name>, e.g. Commands/example/create threshold Bootstrap scripts, rule actions, query console object <directory>_<command name> with spaces replaced by _, invoked with .exec(...): example_create_threshold.exec('thr-2', 'example', '50')

For commands that are not vertex factories extend AbstractOpcCommand and implement runCommand(InvocationContext, String[]).

docs.title: 8. Testing
docs.text:
Plugin tests start a complete in-process namespace with OpcFactory (module waldot-namespace) and the test fixtures of waldot-client; the plugin is discovered from the test class path like in production:

package plugins.example;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import java.nio.file.Files;

import org.apache.tinkerpop.gremlin.structure.Vertex;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import net.rossonet.waldot.api.models.WaldotGraph;
import net.rossonet.waldot.gremlin.opcgraph.strategies.opcua.history.LoggerHistoryStrategy;
import net.rossonet.waldot.gremlin.opcgraph.structure.OpcFactory;
import net.rossonet.waldot.test.WaldotTestEnvironment;

public class ThresholdVertexTest {

    private WaldotGraph g;

    @BeforeEach
    public void beforeEach() throws Exception {
        Files.deleteIfExists(WaldotTestEnvironment.bootFile());
        g = OpcFactory.getOpcGraph(WaldotTestEnvironment.bootUrl(), new LoggerHistoryStrategy());
    }

    @AfterEach
    public void afterEach() throws Exception {
        WaldotTestEnvironment.cleanup(g, null);
    }

    @Test
    public void alarmFollowsValue() {
        final Vertex v = g.addVertex("type", "example:threshold", "label", "t", "limit", "10");
        v.property("value", 20.0);
        assertEquals(true, v.property("alarm").value());
        assertEquals(1L, v.property("exceeded-count").value());
    }
}

See plugins/waldot-plugin-generator/src/test/java for complete examples, including OPC UA client checks with WaldotTestClientHandler. Property writes are processed synchronously, so the assertions can follow the write directly; only values produced by background threads need polling.

docs.title: 9. Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Plugin class annotated with @WaldotPlugin, top-level, public no-arg constructor, in a package under net.rossonet.waldot, plugin or plugins.
  • [ ] Type labels with a unique prefix (vendor:type) to avoid clashes with sim:*, rules:* and other plugins.
  • [ ] Vertex class with the standard constructor, static generateParameters(...), clone().
  • [ ] Lowercase property keys; super.notifyPropertyValueChanging(...) called first.
  • [ ] Threads stopped in close() / notifyRemoveVertex(); plugin state cleared in reset().
  • [ ] Commands created through AbstractCreateVertexCommand with validate(...) for cross-parameter checks.
  • [ ] Compiled for Java 26; extra dependencies shipped in /app/lib.
  • [ ] Behavior verified with an OPC UA client: variables, events, commands.

docs.title: WaldOT User Guide
docs.text:
Operating manual of a WaldOT server with the base plugins (generator, rules engine, TinkerPop server). It explains how the graph is mapped to OPC UA, how to create vertices and edges, how to use the active elements and what to observe while the server runs.

Every example has been executed on the rossonet/waldot image. Step-by-step pages are in Examples.

docs.title: 1. Start the server
docs.text:
docker run -d --name waldot -p 12686:12686 rossonet/waldot:latest
Item Value OPC UA endpoint opc.tcp://<host>:12686/waldot Security anonymous access enabled, user admin / password123 (change them, see Configuration) Bootstrap file /waldot/boot.conf (see Bootstrap) Working directory /app, certificates in /app/.security

With a bootstrap file and a fixed security directory:

docker run -d --name waldot \
  -p 12686:12686 \
  -v "$PWD/boot.conf:/waldot/boot.conf:ro" \
  -v waldot-security:/app/.security \
  rossonet/waldot:latest \
  --anonymous-access false --factory-password "change-me"

Every argument after the image name is a WaldOT option: the complete list is in the Configuration Reference.

The server is ready when the log contains:

INFO BOOT - Bootstrap procedure completed successfully.
INFO WaldOT runner - WaldOT OPC UA Server started successfully

docs.title: 2. The graph in the OPC UA address space
docs.text:
WaldOT is a TinkerPop graph whose vertices and edges are OPC UA nodes.

Objects
├── Gremlin Engine                   root of the graph (ns=2;s=waldot)
│   ├── Vertices
│   │   ├── add vertex               method
│   │   └── <directory>/<subdir>/... folders created by the "directory" property
│   │       └── <vertex>             one object per vertex (ns=2;s=<id>)
│   │           └── <property>       one variable per property
│   ├── Edges
│   └── Variables
└── Commands                         OPC UA methods, grouped by folder
    ├── manage        query, delete directory, edges/...
    ├── information   help, about
    ├── simulator     create generator, create event generator
    ├── rules         create rule, create compute, edges/..., showcase/...
    └── tinkerpop     create gremlin server
Graph element OPC UA vertex id NodeId ns=2;s=<id> (numeric ns=2;i=... when the id is not given) vertex label browse name and display name (cannot be changed) directory property folder under Vertices (plant/pumps → Vertices/plant/pumps) other properties variables of the vertex object; writable from a client edge reference between the two vertex nodes vertex events OPC UA events emitted by the vertex object

Any OPC UA client can browse, read, write and subscribe: UaExpert, Prosys Browser, asyncua (Python), Eclipse Milo, Node-RED.

docs.title: Passive and active elements
docs.text: Kind Created with Behaviour passive vertex no type stores properties, exposed as OPC UA variables active vertex type handled by a plugin runs logic (generates data, evaluates rules, opens a server) passive edge no type relation used by Gremlin traversals active edge type = link-to, link-from, fire, rules:execute propagates values or events between vertices

docs.title: Vertex keys
docs.text: Key Meaning id NodeId identifier, unique label name of the vertex type active type: sim:generator, sim:event-generator, rules:rule, rules:compute, gremlin directory OPC UA folder, levels separated by / any other key property: string, number or boolean. Use lowercase keys.

docs.title: Active types of the base distribution
docs.text:
type Plugin Main properties sim:generator generator algorithm (incremental, decremental, random, sinusoidal, triangular, stopped), min, max, delay (ms); output in data sim:event-generator generator messages (separated by \|), delay, event-type, algorithm (sequential, random, burst, stopped); runtime data, count, severity rules:rule rules engine condition, action (JEXL), hysteresis, debug; counters queue, total, executed, errors rules:compute rules engine threads, execution-timeout-ms, factor; counter queue gremlin TinkerPop Gremlin Server on port (default 1025), bind (default 0.0.0.0)

Complete property tables: generator, rules engine, TinkerPop.

docs.title: Active edges
docs.text:
Edges are created from the source vertex: source.addEdge('<label>', target, 'type', '<edge type>', ...).

type Observes Effect link-to properties of the source copies the value into the target link-from properties of the target copies the value into the source (the source "pulls") fire properties and events of the source sends the change to the target (a rule queues it) rules:execute (compute → rule) the compute executes the rule with the given priority

Properties of link-to, link-from and fire:

Edge property Default Meaning properties-to-monitor all observed properties, separated by ,; * = all <property> = <name> same name rename: 'data', 'level' writes the source data into the target level deadband-value none minimum change to propagate; must be a number (10, not '10') deadband-type absolute absolute or percentage (of the last propagated value) delay 0 the value is written after the given ms active true false disables the edge active-property true false stops property notifications active-event true false stops event notifications (fire) priority 10 priority of the notification (fire)

docs.title: 4. Bootstrap file
docs.text:
The bootstrap file builds the graph at startup and after a reset. It is a JEXL script: statements end with ;, comments are //.

// boot.conf
var gen = graph.addVertex('id', 'level-gen', 'type', 'sim:generator', 'label', 'level-gen',
    'directory', 'plant/sim', 'algorithm', 'sinusoidal', 'min', '0', 'max', '100', 'delay', '200');
var tank = graph.addVertex('id', 'tank-1', 'label', 'tank-1', 'directory', 'plant/tanks', 'level', 0.0);
gen.addEdge('level-signal', tank, 'type', 'link-to', 'properties-to-monitor', 'data', 'data', 'level',
    'deadband-type', 'absolute', 'deadband-value', 10);
log.info('plant ready: ' + cmd.getVerticesCount() + ' vertices');

Syntax, detection of the format, available variables and errors: Bootstrap Configuration.

docs.title: From an OPC UA client: commands
docs.text:
Command Folder Input arguments query manage JEXL expression, e.g. graph.addVertex('id','v1','label','v1') delete directory manage folder NodeId (v:<directory>): removes the OPC UA folder, not the vertices create generator simulator label, directory, algorithm, delay, min, max, post-node-id-data create event generator simulator label, directory and the event generator properties create rule rules label, directory, condition, action, debug, hysteresis create compute rules label, directory, threads, execution-timeout-ms, factor create gremlin server tinkerpop label, directory, port, bind create show case arena / evolution / gas grid rules/showcase see Examples about, help information none

Empty arguments take the default value. Creation commands return the NodeId of the new vertex, or a text starting with error:.

Create edges with the query command (for example g.V().has('id','a').next().addEdge('feeds', g.V().has('id','b').next(), 'type', 'link-to')): the edge commands in manage/edges and rules/edges do not resolve the NodeId arguments correctly in this version.

Example with Python asyncua:

import asyncio
from asyncua import Client, ua

async def main():
    async with Client(url="opc.tcp://127.0.0.1:12686/waldot") as c:
        manage = c.get_node("ns=2;s=c:manage")
        query = ua.NodeId.from_string("ns=2;s=query")
        result = await manage.call_method(query, ua.Variant(
            "graph.addVertex('id','from-opcua','label','from-opcua','directory','opcua')",
            ua.VariantType.String))
        print(result)            # ['v[ns=2;s=from-opcua]', '']
        about = await c.get_node("ns=2;s=c:information").call_method(
            ua.NodeId.from_string("ns=2;s=about"))
        print(about)             # name, description, license, ..., commit, version, branch

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: From the bootstrap or the query command
docs.text:
All commands are available in JEXL as <folder>_<name> objects with an exec(...) method:

var r = simulator_create_generator.exec('cmd-gen', 'plant/sensors', 'incremental', '1000', '0', '10', '');
log.info('created ' + r[0]);

docs.title: From a Gremlin client
docs.text:
Create a gremlin vertex (or run create gremlin server): a TinkerPop Gremlin Server exposes the same graph.

tinkerpop_create_gremlin_server.exec('gremlin-1', 'services', '8182', '0.0.0.0');

docker run -d -p 12686:12686 -p 8182:8182 -v "$PWD/boot.conf:/waldot/boot.conf:ro" rossonet/waldot:latest
curl -X POST -d '{"gremlin":"g.V().count()"}' http://127.0.0.1:8182

The Gremlin Server has no authentication: publish its port only on trusted networks.

docs.title: 6. Rules engine
docs.text:
[source vertex] --fire--> [rules:rule] <--rules:execute-- [rules:compute] --> virtual threads
  1. A property of the source vertex changes; the fire edge notifies the rule.
  2. The rule queues the notification (queue); notifications from the same source within hysteresis ms are discarded.
  3. The compute takes the rules with queued events, highest weight first: weight = priority × factor + queue.
  4. At most threads rules run at the same time; each execution evaluates condition and, when true, runs action.

Variables in condition and action: g, graph, log, cmd, self (the rule vertex), math, rand and all commands. Each execution has its own context: keep state in vertex properties (self.property('n', 1)).

var compute = graph.addVertex('id', 'plant-compute', 'type', 'rules:compute', 'label', 'plant-compute',
    'directory', 'plant/rules', 'threads', '2');
var high = graph.addVertex('id', 'tank-high', 'type', 'rules:rule', 'label', 'tank-high', 'directory', 'plant/rules',
    'condition', "g.V().has('id','tank-1').values('level').next() > 80",
    'action', "g.V().has('id','ctrl-1').next().property('output', 0.0); log.warn('tank-1 high level, valve closed')",
    'hysteresis', '1000');
compute.addEdge('runner', high, 'type', 'rules:execute', 'priority', '100');
tank.addEdge('watch-level', high, 'type', 'fire', 'properties-to-monitor', 'level');

docs.title: Rule counters
docs.text:
Variable Meaning What to check queue notifications waiting grows continuously → compute too slow (raise threads) or hysteresis too low total evaluations does not grow → the fire edge or the rules:execute edge is missing executed actions completed stays at 0 with total growing → condition always false errors compilation or runtime errors grows → read the log, set debug to 2

condition and action can be changed at runtime from a client: the script is compiled again. With debug = 1 every phase is published as an OPC UA event, with debug = 2 it is also written in the log.

docs.title: 7. Monitoring
docs.text:
What Where values of the plant variables of the vertices, OPC UA subscription simulated alarms events of sim:event-generator vertices (subscribe to events of the vertex or of the server) rules health queue, total, executed, errors of each rule; queue of each compute software version about command (name, license, git commit, version, branch) server log docker logs waldot; categories BOOT, CONSOLE, WaldOT runner

Useful queries (query command):

g.V().count().next()
g.V().has('type', 'rules:rule').values('label').toList()
g.V().has('id', 'tank-high').values('errors').next()
g.V().has('id', 'tank-high').inE().toList()
cmd.listCommands()

docs.title: 8. Operations
docs.text:
Task How change the graph at startup edit boot.conf, restart the container rebuild the graph restart the container remove a group of vertices query with a loop, see below run the bootstrap again cmd.reset(): plugins are restarted and the bootstrap runs again, but the existing vertices are not removed keep the OPC UA certificate mount a volume on /app/.security restrict access --anonymous-access false, --factory-password ... disable a command --<cmd>-command-executable false (Configuration)

Remove all the vertices whose id starts with arena-:

var n = 0; for (var v : g.V().toList()) { if (v.id().getIdentifier().toString().startsWith('arena-')) { v.remove(); n = n + 1; } } n;

The graph lives in memory: changes made at runtime are lost at restart unless they are also in the bootstrap file.

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix ambiguous statement error at boot missing ; or Groovy syntax in the bootstrap see Bootstrap Configuration the target of a link-to does not change wrong properties-to-monitor, or deadband too large check the property names; deadband-value must be a number deadband has no effect deadband-value passed as a string use 'deadband-value', 10 rule total stays at 0 missing fire or rules:execute edge check edges with g.V().has('id','<rule>').inE().toList() rule errors grows JEXL error in condition/action set debug to 2 and read the log Vertex with id already exists duplicated id use unique ids already exists from a showcase command the scenario is already in the graph remove its vertices (see Operations) or restart client cannot connect port not published, or wrong host in the endpoint publish -p 12686:12686, set --bind-hostname

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Step-by-step examples for a WaldOT server with the base plugins. Each page can be run on the Docker image: save the script as boot.conf and start

docker run --rm --name waldot -p 12686:12686 \
  -v "$PWD/boot.conf:/waldot/boot.conf:ro" rossonet/waldot:latest

then open opc.tcp://localhost:12686/waldot with an OPC UA client and browse Gremlin Engine/Vertices.

Page Topics 1. Plain vertices vertices, properties, directories, passive edges, Gremlin traversals 2. Active edges link-to, rename, deadband, delay, link-from 3. Generators and rules sim:generator, sim:event-generator, rules:rule, rules:compute, fire, rules:execute 4. Complete bootstrap the previous pages in one file, plugin commands, Gremlin Server 5. Showcase: Dungeon Arena rules with priorities, hysteresis, threads, errors 6. Showcase: Evolution Lab parallel rules, evolutionary algorithm, more than 100 vertices 7. Showcase: Gas Grid PI control loops, deadband and delay on links, safety rules

Scripts use the JEXL syntax described in Bootstrap Configuration: statements end with ;.

docs.title: 1. Plain vertices
docs.text: A plain (passive) vertex has no type: it only stores properties, which are published as OPC UA variables and can be read and written by any client.

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
// 01 - plain vertices
var pump = graph.addVertex('id', 'pump-1', 'label', 'pump-1', 'directory', 'plant/pumps',
    'manufacturer', 'ACME', 'power-kw', 7.5, 'running', true);
var tank = graph.addVertex('id', 'tank-1', 'label', 'tank-1', 'directory', 'plant/tanks', 'level', 0.0);

// passive edge: a relation for traversals, no data flow
pump.addEdge('fills', tank);

log.info('01 out of pump: ' + g.V().has('id', 'pump-1').out('fills').values('label').next());

Log:

INFO CONSOLE - 01 out of pump: tank-1

docs.title: Result in OPC UA
docs.text:
Gremlin Engine/Vertices
└── plant
    ├── pumps
    │   └── pump-1          ns=2;s=pump-1
    │       ├── manufacturer   "ACME"   (String)
    │       ├── power-kw       7.5      (Double)
    │       └── running        true     (Boolean)
    └── tanks
        └── tank-1          ns=2;s=tank-1
            └── level          0.0      (Double)
  • id becomes the NodeId, label the browse name.
  • directory creates the folders plant/pumps and plant/tanks.
  • The value keeps the JEXL type: '7.5' is a String, 7.5 a Double, true a Boolean. The variables are declared as BaseDataType, so a client can write any type.

docs.title: Try
docs.text:
Action Result write running = false from the client the graph property changes: g.V().has('id','pump-1').values('running').next() returns false query: g.V().has('id','tank-1').next().property('level', 12.5) the OPC UA variable level shows 12.5 query: g.V().has('id','tank-1').in('fills').values('label').toList() [pump-1]

Next: 2. Active edges.

docs.title: 2. Active edges
docs.text:
Active edges copy values between vertices when a property changes. They need the vertices of page 1.

Edge Observes Writes link-to source target link-from target source

docs.title: link-to with rename and deadband
docs.text:
// 02 - generator -> tank level, only changes larger than 10
var gen = graph.addVertex('id', 'level-gen', 'type', 'sim:generator', 'label', 'level-gen', 'directory', 'plant/sim',
    'algorithm', 'sinusoidal', 'min', '0', 'max', '100', 'delay', '200');
gen.addEdge('level-signal', tank, 'type', 'link-to', 'properties-to-monitor', 'data', 'data', 'level',
    'deadband-type', 'absolute', 'deadband-value', 10);
  • properties-to-monitor = data: only data of the generator is observed.
  • 'data', 'level': the value is written in level of the tank (rename).
  • deadband-value = 10: a value is propagated only when it differs by more than 10 from the last value of level. It must be a number, not a string.

Observed values (generator every 200 ms):

level-gen.data tank-1.level 27.80 27.80 62.69 62.69 96.00 91.34 (change smaller than 10, not propagated)

With deadband-type = percentage the threshold is a percentage of the last value.

docs.title: link-to with delay
docs.text:
var mirror = graph.addVertex('id', 'tank-1-hmi', 'label', 'tank-1-hmi', 'directory', 'plant/hmi', 'level', 0.0);
tank.addEdge('to-hmi', mirror, 'type', 'link-to', 'properties-to-monitor', 'level', 'delay', 2000);

tank-1-hmi.level follows tank-1.level 2 seconds later: use it to model transport delays (pipes, networks, slow transmitters).

docs.title: link-from
docs.text:
// the valve pulls the command of the controller
var ctrl = graph.addVertex('id', 'ctrl-1', 'label', 'ctrl-1', 'directory', 'plant/ctrl', 'output', 0.0);
var valve = graph.addVertex('id', 'valve-1', 'label', 'valve-1', 'directory', 'plant/valves', 'opening', 0.0);
valve.addEdge('command', ctrl, 'type', 'link-from', 'properties-to-monitor', 'output', 'output', 'opening');
ctrl.property('output', 42.0);
log.info('02 valve opening after link-from: ' + g.V().has('id', 'valve-1').values('opening').next());

INFO CONSOLE - 02 valve opening after link-from: 42.0

The edge goes from the valve to the controller, but the data flows from the controller (output) to the valve (opening). Use link-from when the consumer owns the relation (an actuator reading its setpoint).

docs.title: Edge properties
docs.text:
Property Default Meaning properties-to-monitor all observed properties, separated by ,; * = all <source property> same name name of the destination property deadband-value none minimum change (number) deadband-type absolute absolute or percentage delay 0 ms before writing active true false disables the edge active-property true false stops property notifications

All of them can be changed at runtime, for example from the query command: g.E().hasLabel('to-hmi').next().property('delay', 500).

Next: 3. Generators and rules.

docs.title: 3. Generators and rules
docs.text: This page adds active vertices to the plant of pages 1 and 2: a rule that closes the valve when the tank is too full, and a simulated alarm source.

docs.title: Rule
docs.text:
// 03 - compute + rule + edges
var compute = graph.addVertex('id', 'plant-compute', 'type', 'rules:compute', 'label', 'plant-compute',
    'directory', 'plant/rules', 'threads', '2');
var high = graph.addVertex('id', 'tank-high', 'type', 'rules:rule', 'label', 'tank-high', 'directory', 'plant/rules',
    'condition', "g.V().has('id','tank-1').values('level').next() > 80",
    'action', "g.V().has('id','ctrl-1').next().property('output', 0.0); log.warn('tank-1 high level, valve closed')",
    'hysteresis', '1000');

// the compute executes the rule
compute.addEdge('runner', high, 'type', 'rules:execute', 'priority', '100');
// every change of tank-1.level notifies the rule
tank.addEdge('watch-level', high, 'type', 'fire', 'properties-to-monitor', 'level');

level-gen --link-to--> tank-1 --fire--> tank-high <--rules:execute-- plant-compute
                                            | action
                                            v
                                     ctrl-1.output = 0 --link-from--> valve-1.opening = 0

Log when the level exceeds 80 (the log of a rule writes with the rules engine logger, in the thread of the rule):

[ns=2;s=tank-high] WARN net.rossonet.waldot.rules.WaldotRulesEnginePlugin - tank-1 high level, valve closed

Counters of tank-high after about 20 seconds:

queue total executed errors 0 50 7 0
  • total counts the evaluations (one per notification not discarded by the 1 s hysteresis);
  • executed counts the evaluations with a true condition;
  • errors stays at 0.

docs.title: Try
docs.text: Action Result write condition = false on tank-high executed stops growing; the script is compiled again write debug = 2 every phase of the rule is published as an OPC UA event and logged write threads = 4 on plant-compute up to 4 rules of the compute run at the same time write an invalid condition (g.V() errors grows

docs.title: Event generator
docs.text:
var ev = graph.addVertex('id', 'alarm-sim', 'type', 'sim:event-generator', 'label', 'alarm-sim', 'directory', 'plant/sim',
    'messages', 'pump overload|valve stuck|low pressure', 'delay', '3000', 'event-type', 'device-failure');

Every 3 seconds alarm-sim publishes an OPC UA event of type DeviceFailureEventType with the next message. Subscribe to the events of the vertex with the client. The variables show the last event:

Variable Example data low pressure count 18 severity 351

Events can be sent to other vertices with a fire edge, for example to a rule:

ev.addEdge('alarms', someRule, 'type', 'fire');

docs.title: Generator algorithms
docs.text:
algorithm Values incremental / decremental from min to max (or back) random random between min and max sinusoidal / triangular wave between min and max stopped the last value stays

algorithm, min, max and delay can be changed at runtime.

docs.title: 4. Complete bootstrap
docs.text: The plant of pages 1-3 in one bootstrap file, plus a Gremlin Server opened by a plugin command. This file has been executed as it is.

// --- 03 rule

  -v "$PWD/boot.conf:/waldot/boot.conf:ro" rossonet/waldot:latest

Log:

INFO BOOT - Bootstrap configuration loaded in SCRIPT MODE from URL: [file:///waldot/boot.conf]
INFO CONSOLE - 01 out of pump: tank-1

docs.title: Query the graph with Gremlin
docs.text:
curl -X POST -d '{"gremlin":"g.V().values(\"label\").fold()"}' http://127.0.0.1:8182

... "@value":["tank-1","tank-1-hmi","tank-high","alarm-sim","level-gen","pump-1","ctrl-1","plant-compute","valve-1","gremlin-1"] ...

The Gremlin Server works on the same graph published in OPC UA: a vertex added with Gremlin appears in the address space.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Plugin commands are available as <folder>_<command name> with spaces replaced by _; exec(...) takes the OPC UA input arguments as strings.
  • An error in the script stops it: the vertices created before the error remain. Use try { ... } catch (var e) { ... } for optional parts.
  • cmd.reset() runs the file again without removing the existing vertices: creating the same ids fails with Vertex with id already exists.

Next: 5. Showcase: Dungeon Arena.

docs.title: 5. Showcase: Dungeon Arena
docs.text: A small tower-defense game made only of generators, edges and rules. It shows priorities, two computes with a different number of threads, hysteresis, debug and a rule that always fails.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
From an OPC UA client: Commands/rules/showcase/create show case arena. From a bootstrap or the query command:

log.info(create_show_case_arena.exec('')[0]);

show case arena created: 3 generators, 4 state vertices, 2 compute, 7 rules
Argument Default Meaning delay-ms 250 (minimum 10) period of the generators; the turn clock uses twice this value

A second call answers show case arena already exists: remove its vertices before creating it again.

docs.text:
Values after about one minute:

Vertex Values arena-tower hp 72, kills 3, spells 31 arena-wave difficulty 7 arena-player level 1, gold 110, score 170, defeats 4 Rule total executed errors arena-rule-spawn-wave 255 42 0 arena-rule-tower-damage 255 100 0 arena-rule-fire-spell 128 31 0 arena-rule-game-over 104 4 0 arena-rule-turn-tick 127 13 0 arena-rule-level-up 35 5 0 arena-rule-broken 127 0 127

Next: 6. Showcase: Evolution Lab.

docs.title: 6. Showcase: Evolution Lab
docs.text: An evolutionary algorithm written as rules. Each individual of the population is a vertex; one rule per individual mutates it in parallel; a second compute with one thread runs selection, crossover and statistics. The goal is to maximise 100 - Rastrigin(x, y, z) (maximum 100 at 0, 0, 0).

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
From an OPC UA client: Commands/rules/showcase/create show case evolution. From a bootstrap or the query command:

log.info(create_show_case_evolution.exec('', '', '', '')[0]);

show case evolution created: 40 individuals, 42 generators, 2 compute, 46 rules, 4 control vertices
Argument Default Range Meaning population-size 40 30-1000 individuals (vertices = 3 × N + 14) delay-ms 200 ≥ 10 period of the generators target-fitness 99 fitness that stops the evolution seed 42 seed of the initial population

docs.title: Graph (folder rules/showcase/evolution)
docs.text:
Folder Content population evo-ind-0 ... evo-ind-N: genes x, y, z, fitness, data (noise) generators one random generator per individual (mutation noise, link-to into data), evo-gen-clock (generations), evo-gen-rate (mutation rate 5-50) rules/evaluate evo-rule-evaluate-i: when the noise is below the mutation rate, mutates the genes and keeps the mutation only if the fitness improves rules/breeding evo-rule-select-best, evo-rule-crossover, evo-rule-stagnation, evo-rule-converged, evo-rule-stats (debug = 1), evo-rule-bad-input (fails on purpose) compute evo-eval-pool (8 threads, evaluation rules), evo-breeding (1 thread, breeding rules) control evo-hall-of-fame, evo-generation, evo-mutation-rate, evo-stats

Breeding priorities: converged 190, crossover 150, stagnation 100, stats 80, bad-input 60, select-best 50. select-best is the most frequent rule, so it has a low priority: with one thread the others must not starve.

docs.title: What to observe
docs.text:
Values after about one minute (40 individuals):

Vertex Values evo-hall-of-fame fitness 97.8 at x 1.0, y 0.96, z 0.01; improvements 11; stagnations 4; status running evo-stats mean 91.46, best 97.8, worst 83.13 evo-mutation-rate data 21.6, boost 30 Rule queue total executed errors evo-rule-select-best 1 281 281 0 evo-rule-crossover 0 64 22 0 evo-rule-stagnation 0 64 5 0 evo-rule-stats 0 64 64 0 evo-rule-converged 0 11 0 0 evo-rule-bad-input 0 64 0 64 evo-rule-evaluate-0 0 320 122 0
  • evo-hall-of-fame.fitness grows over time; status becomes converged when it reaches target-fitness and the generators stop.
  • stagnations and evo-mutation-rate.boost grow when the best does not improve: the mutation rate increases to escape local maxima (here the algorithm is near the local maximum at x ≈ 1, y ≈ 1).
  • queue of evo-rule-select-best is often 1: the single thread of evo-breeding is busy.

docs.title: Try
docs.text:
Action Effect evo-eval-pool.threads = 1 evaluations are serialized, queue of the evaluate rules grows evo-breeding.threads = 4 breeding rules run in parallel evo-gen-rate.algorithm = stopped the mutation rate is fixed evo-rule-converged.condition = true at its next notification the rule sets status = converged and stops all generators

Next: 7. Showcase: Gas Grid.

docs.title: 7. Showcase: Gas Grid
docs.text:
A gas distribution network controlled by PI loop controllers written as rules. It is designed for demos to gas utilities: plants, transmitters, valves and controllers are vertices; measurements travel on link-to/link-from edges with deadband and delay; control and safety logic are rules.

The model is didactic, not a hydraulic simulation: the process is a first-order system and all values (pressures, demands, thresholds, delays) are indicative.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
From an OPC UA client: Commands/rules/showcase/create show case gas grid. From a bootstrap or the query command:

log.info(create_show_case_gas_grid.exec('', '', '', '', '', '')[0]);

show case gas grid created: 4 stations, gas metano, 58 vertices
Argument Default Range Meaning stations 4 2-20 pressure reduction stations delay-ms 200 ≥ 10 simulation step setpoint 25 5-100 downstream pressure (mbar) pipe-delay-ms 300 0-10000 dead time of the pipe gas-type metano metano, metano-blu gas profile compare true true, false the last station has no deadband, for comparison

Invalid arguments create nothing (argument 'stations' must be between 2 and 20). Vertices: 14 + 11 × stations.

docs.title: Gas profiles (indicative values)
docs.text:
Parameter metano metano-blu (20 % hydrogen) relative density 0.60 0.48 flow factor at the same opening 1.00 1.12 nominal demand 50 57.5 ESD threshold over the setpoint +30 % +25 % transmitter deadband 2.0 mbar 1.2 mbar demand deadband 5 % 3 % upstream pressure deadband 0.3 bar 0.2 bar dead time pipe-delay-ms × 1.0 pipe-delay-ms × 1.2

The profile is stored on the gas-network vertex.

docs.text:
supply/         gas-gate-gen (upstream pressure), gas-clock (simulation step), gas-scan (scan cycle)
transmission/   gas-trunk (high pressure line)
stations/
  station-i/    gas-sensor-i, gas-valve-i, gas-ctrl-i, gas-plant-i
consumers/      gas-consumer-i + gas-demand-gen-i (demand profile)
safety/         gas-leak-monitor
supervisory/    gas-network (profile, network setpoint, load), gas-stats
rules/
  control/      gas-rule-pi-i, gas-rule-mode-guard-i
  safety/       gas-rule-esd-trip-i, gas-rule-esd-reset-i, gas-rule-leak-detect
  process/      gas-rule-plant-i
  supervisory/  gas-rule-balancer, gas-rule-stats, gas-rule-bad-sensor
compute/        gas-control-loop, gas-process, gas-supervisory
links/          link-to and link-from edges
triggers/       fire edges
Vertex Main properties Role gas-plant-i pressure, upstream simulated process: the real downstream pressure gas-sensor-i pressure transmitter: sees the pressure with dead time and deadband gas-ctrl-i setpoint, mode, fault, integral, output, bias, kp, ki, esd-trips loop controller state gas-valve-i opening (0-100 %) control valve gas-consumer-i demand demand of the station

docs.title: Data flow of a station
docs.text:
gas-gate-gen --link-to--> gas-trunk --link-to--> gas-plant-i.upstream
gas-demand-gen-i --link-to--> gas-consumer-i.demand
                     rule "plant" (valve opening, upstream, demand) -> gas-plant-i.pressure
gas-plant-i.pressure --link-to (delay + deadband)--> gas-sensor-i.pressure --fire--> PI / guard / ESD rules
gas-network.setpoint --link-to--> gas-ctrl-i.setpoint
gas-ctrl-i.output --link-from (deadband 0.5 %)--> gas-valve-i.opening --> rule "plant"

The loop is closed: the valve changes the pressure, the transmitter sees it later, the controller corrects the valve.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Fired by Condition Action gas-rule-pi-i sensor.pressure and scan cycle mode AUTO error, integral with anti-windup, output 0-100 % gas-rule-mode-guard-i sensor.pressure fault state changes measure < 0 or > 200: fault = sensor, mode MANUAL; back to AUTO with a valid measure gas-rule-esd-trip-i sensor.pressure pressure > setpoint × (1 + ESD margin) mode ESD, output 0, esd-trips +1 gas-rule-esd-reset-i sensor.pressure mode ESD and pressure < 50 % of the setpoint back to AUTO gas-rule-plant-i clock always process model gas-rule-balancer clock always network setpoint from the mean demand (hysteresis 1 s) gas-rule-stats clock always mean error, mean opening, total ESD trips (hysteresis 1 s) gas-rule-leak-detect mean opening mean opening > 90 % changes the alarm state alarm = leak / none gas-rule-bad-sensor clock reads a missing transmitter fails on purpose: errors grows

PI controller: error = setpoint - pressure, output = clamp(bias + kp·error + ki·integral, 0, 100) with kp = 0.4, ki = 0.1; the integral is not updated when the output is saturated.

Process model, at every clock step: target = 0.9 · opening · (upstream / 24) · flow_factor - 0.25 · (demand - nominal) - 0.25 · leak / stations, pressure = pressure + 0.3 · (target - pressure).

Compute Threads Rules (priority) Why gas-control-loop 1 ESD trip (300), guard (250), ESD reset (200), PI (100) controllers must not overlap, safety first gas-process 4 plant models (100) independent, in parallel gas-supervisory 1 leak (60), balancer (50), stats (40), bad-sensor (10) slow logic, low priority

Safety rules have no hysteresis: a discarded notification could hide an overpressure.

docs.text:
Values after about one minute with the defaults:

Station sensor.pressure ctrl.setpoint ctrl.mode ctrl.output valve.opening PI total 0 (deadband) 23.76 25.2 AUTO 29.1 28.95 138 3 (no deadband) 24.51 25.2 AUTO 30.19 30.36 398
  • The pressure follows the setpoint; valve.opening follows ctrl.output through the link-from edge.
  • Station 3 has no deadband: its PI rule is evaluated about three times more often for the same regulation.
  • gas-stats: mean-abs-error 2.75, mean-opening 29.44, esd-trips 0.
  • gas-rule-bad-sensor: errors = total, executed = 0 (JEXL exceptions in the log are expected for this rule).

docs.title: Live interventions
docs.text:
Verified on the default scenario:

Intervention Result write 90 on gas-sensor-1.pressure immediately gas-ctrl-1.mode = ESD, output = 0, esd-trips = 1; the other stations stay AUTO; after a few seconds the pressure falls and the controller is back in AUTO write -5 on gas-sensor-1.pressure fault = sensor, mode MANUAL until the next valid measure from the plant (a few hundred ms) write 600 on gas-leak-monitor.leak the valves open to compensate; when gas-stats.mean-opening exceeds 90 % (about 40 s) gas-leak-monitor.alarm = leak; write 0 to cancel write 40 on gas-network.base-setpoint the balancer distributes the new setpoint (41.2 with the current demand) to all controllers; the pressures follow (43.8 after 25 s) change kp, ki of gas-ctrl-i faster or more oscillating response change deadband-value or delay of the edge pipe-to-transmitter-i more or fewer PI executions, more or less oscillation write MANUAL on gas-ctrl-i.mode the PI rule stops acting gas-demand-gen-i.algorithm = stopped the demand stays constant

docs.title: Rules engine concepts in the demo
docs.text: Concept Where condition / action PI, guard, ESD, leak fire edge triggers/: the measure fires the controllers rules:compute with threads 1 thread for the loops, 4 for the process rules:execute with priority ESD (300) before PI (100) hysteresis balancer and statistics (1 s) counters queue, total, executed, errors on every rule runtime changes setpoint, kp, ki, deadband-value, delay

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• No pressure losses, line pack, temperature or real gas composition.
  • Upstream pressure is fixed around 24 bar with a slow oscillation.
  • The PI is discrete with a variable step (executions depend on events) and is not tuned for a real plant.
  • metano-blu changes only some coefficients (flow, demand, thresholds, delay).

To create the scenario again restart the server or remove the gas-... vertices (see Operations). Tests: WaldotRulesEngineGasGridTest.
